si_3_author_journal_year: Richard A. I. Bethlehem et al., Communications Biology, 2020
si_4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

dc_1_datasets_using.detail: The study utilized pooled data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and II datasets.
dc_1_datasets_using.supporting_text: we utilized the ABIDE datasets (ABIDE I and II; 15)

answer.ABIDE (I+II): normative training (TD males) and clinical atypicality detection (ASD males)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Typically developing (TD) males were used to construct the LOESS-based normative models, while individuals with autism (ASD) were compared against these norms to compute individualized w-scores (atypicality metrics).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Normative modelling of age-related CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group (TD)... These statistical norms were then used to compute a w-score... for every individual with autism

dc_3_hc_number.detail: A final sample of 624 typically developing males was used for the normative model after excluding individuals based on age-binning constraints and quality criteria.

dc_5_sex_info.detail: The normative model was restricted to males due to insufficient data for females across age bins and known sex-differential effects.
dc_5_sex_info.supporting_text: we conducted normative modelling on the male group only (Fig. 2a).
